news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse treasury investments earned £6.4m in 2025-26, £2.1m above budget
news_drafts.lead:
Vale of White Horse District Council earned £6.401m from investing its spare cash in 2025-26, against a budget of £4.342m. That is £2.059m more than planned, according to the council's treasury activities report for the year, which went to its Cabinet on 9 October 2026 and is among the papers for the Council meeting of 21 October.

Treasury management is how a council borrows, invests its spare cash and manages the risks of both. The report says the extra income was "primarily due to longer sustained levels of higher interest rates throughout the year and higher balances than forecast". Interest rates stayed higher for longer than the budget had assumed, and the council held more cash than it had forecast. The report puts the rate of return achieved at £2.1 million higher than the original budget.

The papers give no breakdown of how the £2.059m was used, and no figure for what the council expects to earn in the current year. The council's income from its investments in 2025-26 is reported here as a single outturn figure, meaning the actual result once the year had ended, set against the budget.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix D - Vale Treasury activities 2025-26, 09/10/2026 Cabinet

news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse plans to use £3.6m of reserves in 2027/28 against a sustainable £2.9m
news_drafts.lead:
Vale of White Horse District Council's medium-term financial plan (MTFP) projects it will draw £3.6m from its reserves, the money it has put aside, in 2027/28. The sustainable level is £2.9m, leaving a shortfall of £754,000. The figures are in the budget-setting report going to the council's Cabinet on 9 October 2026.

The gap widens in later years, according to the plan the council agreed in February 2026. The shortfall against the sustainable level is projected at £2.1m in 2028/29, £3.3m in 2029/30 and £4.8m in 2030/31. The report says the amount expected to be used in 2027/28 "was much higher than that needed in 2026/27 and would not be in line with the recommended parameters, based on current estimates". Beyond that year, it says, use of reserves "was projected to continue to be unsustainable and outside of the parameters set".

The report says "action will be required by the council to address the increasing budget gap". It adds that the pause in local government reorganisation, the restructuring of councils in the area, means the council now has to deal with the gap sooner than it first expected.
news_drafts.paper_title: VALE Cabinet budget setting report Oct 2026

news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse: all eight key financial audits rated Substantial; cyber security rated Limited
news_drafts.lead:
All eight of the Vale of White Horse's key financial control audits for 2025/26 were completed with a "Substantial" assurance rating, the Joint Audit and Governance Committee was told on 6 October. The audits covered accounts payable, accounts receivable, council tax, the general ledger, business rates, treasury management (how the council borrows and invests its cash), payroll, and housing benefit and council tax reduction claims. Together they produced five management actions, all the lowest priority, and none rated Priority 1 or 2.

The internal audit and risk manager's overall opinion on 2024/25 was that there was "a satisfactory system of governance, risk, internal control", with enhancements recommended in some areas. One audit went the other way: cyber security, including artificial intelligence, was rated "Limited", which the papers say means significant improvement is needed. It produced nine management actions, two of them Priority 1 (fundamental to service integrity), five Priority 2 and two Priority 3.

The external auditor, Bishop Fleming, disclaimed the 2024/25 accounts for both councils, meaning it did not give an opinion on them, as part of wider problems across local audit. Its roadmap aims for qualified accounts for 2025/26 and unqualified for 2026/27, subject to satisfactory progress on "build back" work. The committee also said the number of overdue internal audit recommendations had been "excessive", and recent reports show it falling. Three audits were deferred from the 2025/26 plan: two pending the Ocella replacement project, and one moved to 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: Appendix D - Vale Treasury activities 2025-26, 09/10/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Investment property portfolio fell in value from £3.97m to £3.44m; rental income declined from £0.22m to £0.19m
findings.detail: The council's portfolio of investment properties (land, offices and shops let on a commercial basis) had an average net book value of £3.44m at 31 March 2026, down from £3.97m the prior year. Rental income also fell from £0.22m to £0.19m, though the gross return achieved was 5.4%.
findings.matters: Property valuations and rental income are material to financial planning; the decline in both value and income requires monitoring to understand asset base trends
findings.figures: Property values: £3.97m (2025) → £3.44m (2026); rental income: £0.22m → £0.19m; gross return 5.4%
findings.quote: These assets are valued on an annual basis and had an average net book value of £3.44 million at 31 March 2026 (£3.97 million as at 31 March 2025). Income generated was £0.19 million (£0.22 million in 2025/26).

findings.paper_title: Appendix D - Vale Treasury activities 2025-26, 09/10/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Council outperformed MUFG Benchmarking club peers by 0.40 basis points with low-risk investment profile
findings.detail: The council participated in the MUFG Benchmarking club and outperformed the group average by 0.40 basis points while maintaining a very low-risk investment profile, with holdings concentrated in local authorities and money market funds.
findings.matters: Shows the council ranks competitively among comparable authorities for treasury performance while managing risk conservatively
findings.quote: The Council is part of the MUFG Benchmarking club and performed well amongst its peers. The council outperformed the average of the group by 0.40 basis points with a very low risk profile of investments, mainly with local authorities and money market funds.

findings.paper_title: Appendix D - Vale Treasury activities 2025-26, 09/10/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Council's treasury deposit returns of 4.30% beat SONIA benchmark of 3.94% by 36 basis points
findings.detail: The council achieved an average rate of return of 4.30% on internally managed treasury deposits, outperforming the three-month SONIA benchmark of 3.94% by 0.36 percentage points. The CCLA property fund also outperformed its benchmark, returning 4.35% against a 4.01% target.
findings.matters: Demonstrates active portfolio management and competitive performance; the 36 basis point outperformance on substantial average cash balances represents significant value creation
findings.figures: 4.30%, 3.94%, 0.36 percentage points; CCLA 4.35% vs 4.01% benchmark, 0.34% outperformance
findings.quote: The actual average rate of return on internally managed treasury deposits for the year was 4.30 per cent

findings.paper_title: Appendix D - Vale Treasury activities 2025-26, 09/10/2026 Cabinet
findings.headline: Treasury investment income exceeded budget by £2.059m, driven by sustained higher interest rates
findings.detail: The council earned £6.401m in treasury investment income in 2025-26, against a budget of £4.342m. The outperformance of £2.059m was primarily due to longer sustained levels of higher interest rates throughout the year and higher cash balances than forecast.
findings.matters: Shows the council captured the benefit of the higher interest rate environment; other finance directors need to know how sustained rate conditions affected rate-dependent revenue forecasts
findings.quote: The actual rate of return achieved was £2.1 million higher than the original budget. This is primarily due to longer sustained levels of higher interest rates throughout the year and higher balances than forecast

findings.headline: Internal audit opinion for 2025/26 satisfactory, with three of 22 audits receiving limited assurance ratings
findings.detail: The 2024/25 internal audit opinion was reported as satisfactory for governance, risk and control arrangements. During 2025/26, 22 audits were undertaken as part of the internal audit plan. Only three audits received limited assurance ratings, indicating overall findings were largely satisfactory with identified enhancements needed in specific areas.
findings.matters: Internal audit findings demonstrate whether the council's governance and internal controls are effective; a satisfactory overall opinion with only three limited assurance ratings across 22 audits indicates controls are generally effective with some areas for improvement.
findings.figures: 22 audits undertaken in 2025/26; 3 limited assurance ratings; 19 satisfactory or better
findings.quote: the internal audit and risk manager reported that she reached the overall opinion that there was a satisfactory system of governance, risk, internal control. Findings indicate that overall, arrangements were satisfactory, although some enhancements have been recommended.
